result.reason:
The finding holds on its main points, so refuted is false. I rebuilt the statewide base vectors offline from the current worktree code into a skeptic store copy and read the band files back. Band files carry no piece size and no feature id: encode() writes only k, n, z, l, s, d and g, and a probe piece with a size comes out without it. The P2 integration notes (lines 140 to 142) say the band files carry each piece's length and that a name is labelled once per view on its largest piece. The first part is false. The rule also fails in substance: the once-per-view rule would hide separate features (147 of the 163 name and zoom combinations with two or more label points have label points more than 1 km apart; Big Lake at zoom 8 has two lakes 220 km apart), and the largest piece of a split area lacked its label in two statewide cases, because the label goes only to the piece whose box holds it (basemap2.py line 1342).

Three parts of the finding need correcting. Band A carries d and s keys too, so the claim that its keys are only g, k, l, n, z is wrong. The browser could derive length and area from each piece's rings, so "cannot be applied" is too strong; the river and route rule does need a size, but a feature id is not needed, because each area has one label point and each joined river is one feature. And 16 combinations have label points under 1 km apart (Benton Lake ponds, Intake Dam Fishing Access Site), which may be parcel or duplicate records where one label is right, so "separate features" holds for records, not always for places. The proposed source OBJECTID conflicts with the module's attribute rule (docstring lines 8 and 9) and with the key allow-list that verify enforces (lines 172 and 1866); a build-local index avoids both.

This is a defect in the handoff, not in shipped pages: basemap2.py has not changed since 00:37 UTC, and neither map.js nor build.py reads hail/base yet. Medium is a fair rating. For the owner of the integration notes: remove the claim that band files carry size, or add size (river and route pieces need it, since lines have no label point); say the label sits on the single piece that holds it, which need not be the largest; and drop the once-per-view rule for areas, or merge same-name labels by distance in Python. Add a test that reads the encoded file, because the existing size test checks in-memory pieces only. Tests: tests.test_basemap2 passes (57 tests). The whole suite ran 2,234 tests with 6 failures and 12 skips; the six failures are the push-path and offline-line checks in test_website_workflow.py that the P2 report already lists as integrator-owned, and nothing else failed.
